newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel says tax reform to boost jobs, growth.
newsitem.headline: Waigel says tax reform to boost jobs, growth.

text.p: Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Thursday that his plan to reform the German tax system would boost corporate investment, leading to faster growth and more job creation.

Waigel was speaking as he entered a meeting of leaders from his Christian Social Union (CSU) to review a coalition reform deal to knock 30 billion marks off German taxes by 1999. Waigel will unveil the reform later.

Waigel has alreay dubbed the reform the biggest in the history of post-war Germany, but although the coalition has agreed on cuts in income and corporate taxation, the question of an offsetting increase in value-added tax is still open.
Chancellor Helmut Kohl, speaking before a separate meeting of his Christian Democrat party (CDU), praised the tax plan.
Responding to critics from both the opposition and within his own party, Kohl said they should first come up with "a proposal of this scale which also has such a positive impact on small incomes."
Kohl said he wanted to begin talks as soon as possible with Germany's federal states and municipal authorities on the reform package.
Extensive consultations will be needed before legislation can be introduced to parliament. The Finance Ministry said the legislative process could last all year and even run into 1998.
